Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

each other pronoun

also one another, mutually, together (with each other)

classical

Cic. Att. 6.1.12: Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē
Cic. Att. 14.13B.5: ut nōsmet ipsī inter nōs conjūnctiōrēs sīmus (Lewis & Short, s.v. conjungō)
Traupman 354

inter sē (inter nōs, inter vōs)

phrase: inter with the reflexive, or with nōs, vōs

each other, one another

The classical way, with any verb: amant inter sē, they love each other; inter nōs for us, inter vōs for you.

Other words

  • alter alterum — each other (of two)

    phrase: alter twice, the second in the case the verb needs · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 7.11: alter alterī theātrum sumus; Liv. 30.30.2: alter alterīus cōnspectū

    alter alterī theātrum sumus, we are an audience for each other. Of more than two, alius alium.

  • alius alium — one another (of more than two)

    phrase: alius twice · also used · classical · Liv. 2.10.9: dum alius alium … circumspectant

  • invicem — each other, mutually

    adverb · also used · classical · Quint. 1.3.11: positīs invicem … quaestiunculīs; Plin. Ep. 4.1.2: invicem amāre (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    In this sense from Livy on, mostly post-Augustan (Pliny, Tacitus, Quintilian), not in Cicero; classically it means “in turn” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur, sed discunt, alter … frēnīs eget, alter calcāribus

    The boys Cicero love each other, they play together, but they learn too; one … needs the reins, the other the spurs.Cic. Att. 6.1.12

  • vetus verbum hoc quidem est: commūnia esse amīcōrum inter sē omnia

    It’s an old saying, at any rate, that friends have everything in common with each other.Ter. Ad. 803–804

  • satis enim magnum alter alterī theātrum sumus

    For we are a big enough audience for each other.Sen. Ep. 7.11

  • paulisper alter alterīus cōnspectū, admīrātiōne mūtuā prope attonitī, conticuēre

    For a little while, each at the sight of the other, almost stunned with mutual admiration, they fell silent.Liv. 30.30.2

  • cūnctātī aliquamdiū sunt, dum alius alium, ut proelium incipiant, circumspectant

    They hung back for some time, while each looked round at the others to start the fight.Liv. 2.10.9

  • sunt etiam nōnnūllī acuendīs puerōrum ingeniīs nōn inūtilēs lūsūs, cum positīs invicem cujusque generis quaestiunculīs aemulantur

    There are also some games, not useless for sharpening children’s wits, when they compete by setting each other little questions of every kind.Quint. 1.3.11

  • frīgoribus partō agricolae plērumque fruuntur mūtuaque inter sē laetī convīvia cūrant. invītat geniālis hiems cūrāsque resolvit

    In the cold the farmers mostly enjoy what they have earned, and, happy, give dinners for each other in turn; festive winter invites them and loosens their cares.Verg. G. 1.300–302

  • Inter sē amplexī sunt.

    They embraced one another.Traupman 354

See also themselves, ourselves, they.
